rawFindings.title: Incorrect detection of missing or unexpected trailing comma in 'always-multiline' option
rawFindings.explanation: The patch replaces the variable lastTokenOnNewLine (which checks if the last token comma is on a new line) with nodeIsMultiLine that checks if the node itself is multiline. This modifies the condition to report errors for dangling commas based on node multiline state instead of token position. This fixes the rule for cases where comma is on the same line but node spans multiple lines, correcting error reporting for trailing commas under 'always-multiline' option.
rawFindings.suggestion: On line 42, define nodeIsMultiLine as var nodeIsMultiLine = node.loc.start.line !== node.loc.end.line; use nodeIsMultiLine instead of lastTokenOnNewLine in lines 44-46 in conditions for reporting missing or unexpected trailing commas under 'always-multiline' option.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect multiline check for trailing comma enforcement in comma-dangle rule
rawFindings.explanation: The code replaces the check 'lastTokenOnNewLine' with a new variable 'nodeIsMultiLine' which compares node.loc.start.line and node.loc.end.line directly. However, the old code checked if the penultimateToken was on a different line from the node end (lastTokenOnNewLine), which is more precise for trailing comma placement. By only checking the node multiline status, it might incorrectly enforce trailing comma requirements in some cases, especially when the last item and the closing bracket are on
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the precise check of whether the penultimate token is on a different line from the node's end token instead of only relying on node's multiline status. Revert lines 42-47 to use lastTokenOnNewLine = node.loc.end.line !== penultimateToken.loc.end.line and use that for the conditional checks to ensure accurate enforcement of trailing commas in multiline contexts.
